title: Temperance Tarot Card Meaning: Upright, Reversed & Love
description: Temperance upright: balance, patience; reversed: extremes or impatience. Love, work, advice, Waite's 1911 text and the 1909 card. Draw it for your question.
image_alt: Temperance, 1909 Rider–Waite–Smith card: a winged angel in a white robe pours a stream between two gold cups, one foot in a pool, with a path leading to mountains and a yellow light.
capsule: Temperance, card XIV, stands for balance, moderation and patience: the slow blending of things that seem opposed. Reversed, the mix tips into extremes or hurry. It is a steadying card whose one caution is against forcing the pace. For a yes or no question, upright means yes, since the parts are settling into place without strain.

blocks.heading: What is on the Temperance card?
paragraphs: A tall angel in a white robe stands at the edge of a pool and pours a stream from one cup into another. Waite describes "a winged angel, with the sign of the sun upon his forehead", and then corrects himself: "I speak of him in the masculine sense, but the figure is neither male nor female" (p. 124). What flows between the cups, he says, is "the essences of life", passed "from chalice to chalice" (p. 124).

One foot rests in the water and the other on the bank, which for Waite shows "the nature of the essences" (p. 124). On the 1909 card the wings, in red and dark tones, spread almost from edge to edge and are the largest shapes on the card. The hair is yellow, a gold disc sits on the forehead, and on the breast is a square with a triangle inside, Waite's "square and triangle of the septenary" (p. 124). XIV is printed at the top, and tall yellow flowers rise from the reeds on the right.

On the left a path climbs from the water toward far mountains. Waite writes of "a direct path" up to the heights, and above it "a great light, through which a crown is seen vaguely" (p. 124). On the 1909 card that light is a yellow glow over the peaks.

blocks.heading: What did Waite write about Temperance?
paragraphs: In plain words, the upright list is practical: spending with care, keeping to the middle, running things well, making room for others. The reversed list opens with churches and the priesthood, a side of the card Arcana Diary does not read, and closes with things that refuse to mix: disunion, unfortunate combinations, competing interests.

Waite thought the old name a poor fit. He wrote that "the entire symbol has no especial connexion with Temperance" (p. 24), and later explained why it is called so "fantastically": under its rule the figure "tempers, combines and harmonises the psychic and material natures" (p. 127).

blocks.heading: What does Temperance mean upright?
paragraphs: Upright, Temperance points to balance found slowly: blending two sides of a situation, two needs, or two parts of yourself until they work together. It tends to appear when you are tempted to swing hard one way, and it offers the middle path instead.

Moderation here does not mean standing still. The angel keeps the stream moving between both cups; nothing stops and nothing is wasted. Patience is the working tool: steady, small adjustments rather than one dramatic fix. The result is rarely spectacular, but it holds.

The card also favors combining what already works instead of starting from zero: an old skill with a new setting, rest with effort, your needs with someone else's. If this fits your situation, ask yourself: where am I trying to rush something that only works at its own pace?

blocks.heading: What does Temperance mean reversed?
paragraphs: Reversed, Temperance shows a mix out of proportion: too much of one thing and too little of another, or impatience with a process that cannot be hurried. You might catch yourself going to extremes, all or nothing, with no setting in between.

The end of Waite's reversed list, disunion and competing interests, sits close to this reading: parts that pull against each other instead of blending. Reading this side as excess and hurry is modern, not Waite's.
This imbalance does not call for a full overhaul. Pick one area that has tipped too far and bring it a little back toward the center; the rest often follows.

blocks.heading: What does Temperance mean in love?
paragraphs: In love, Temperance offers a gentle middle ground. If you are single, it can point to a calmer pace: getting to know someone without racing ahead, and keeping your own life in balance while you do.
In a relationship, the card speaks of give and take: where you could soften, and where you need to stay true to what you need. It describes your share of the blend.
Reversed in love, it may show a rhythm that swings between very close and very distant. What small change would bring it back toward the middle?

blocks.heading: What does Temperance mean for work and money?
paragraphs: At work, Temperance favors steady progress over bursts of overtime: combining skills, blending a team's ideas, pacing a long project. It can point to a role where you are the one who brings people together.
With money, look at your own approach. Waite's list for this card opens with "economy, moderation, frugality" (p. 285); the modern reading is simply to avoid extremes in how you spend or save.
Reversed, notice where work or spending has turned into all or nothing.

blocks.heading: What is Temperance's advice?
paragraphs: Pick one area of life where you tend to overdo or underdo things and move it a notch toward the middle. Temperance does not ask for a new regime, only one small correction you can keep up. After a while, notice how the rest of the mix responds.

blocks.heading: Is Temperance a yes or no card?
Temperance as a person and as a feeling
paragraphs: In a spread, Temperance often stands for the go-between: someone patient who finds the workable middle and helps different sides meet. When the card points at you, it shows your ability to stay steady while things settle. Its emotional tone is calm and unhurried; reversed, it turns restless, pulled between two extremes.

pairs.text: Balance in motion. Keep juggling, but decide which demand gets the steady pour first.
Two people meeting halfway. Give and take in proportions that feel fair to you.
Friction meets patience. Look for the idea that can hold the clashing views together.
Gentle power and an even pace. Quiet persistence will carry you further than force.

blocks.heading: Temperance or The Star?
paragraphs: Both cards show a figure pouring water with a foot in it. In The Star the figure kneels: "Her left knee is on the land and her right foot upon the water", and she pours from two ewers onto "sea and land" (p. 136). Temperance stands and passes the stream between two cups held in the air. The Star is hope and renewal after a hard stretch; Temperance is the patient work of blending, a balance built step by step. One restores, the other adjusts.

blocks.heading: Questions to ask yourself about Temperance
paragraphs: Where in my life am I swinging between too much and too little?
What two things am I trying to blend, and what pace do they need?
What small adjustment could I keep up without strain?

faq.q: Is Temperance a good or bad card?
faq.a: Good, in a quiet way. It backs patience, steady effort and the knack of bringing opposites together. Its only warning is against forcing results. Because it is so calm, it is easy to overlook in a spread, yet it often marks the point where things begin to settle.

faq.q: Does Temperance mean I have to give something up?
faq.a: Not necessarily. The word suggests abstaining to many people, but the picture shows mixing, not refusing: the liquid moves from cup to cup. Waite himself felt the name had little to do with the image (p. 24). The card asks for proportion, which sometimes means less of something and sometimes more.

faq.q: What number is Temperance in tarot?
faq.a: Temperance is card XIV, number 14 of the Major Arcana, placed between Death and The Devil. Waite gives it the same number, 14, in his survey of the trumps in Part I (p. 24).

faq.q: Does Temperance show how someone sees me?
faq.a: No. On Arcana Diary no card describes what goes on in another person's mind. What it can show is your side: whether you are giving and asking in proportion, and how patient you are with the pace of things. A more useful question is what balance you want.

waite.quote: Economy, moderation, frugality, management, accommodation. Reversed: Things connected with churches, religions, sects, the priesthood … also disunion, unfortunate combinations, competing interests.
